source.name: MHCLG, Review of local government reorganisation launched, 7 September 2026

items.title: Spending Review, which confirms the detailed arrangements for retained income tax
items.why: The Cabinet Statement says the Spending Review confirms the income tax share arrangements, so half of the fiscal devolution answer may sit beyond the Budget. Placed in 2027 by the Keep Britain Working update. No date is published.

source.name: DWP, Keep Britain Working: a national growth opportunity, 23 September 2026, and Cabinet Office, Rewiring the State, 31 July 2026

items.title: Casey Commission reports on how to build a National Care Service
items.why: Free personal care for older people is planned for the next Parliament, funded by adjusting the Triple Lock from April 2030. Adult social care is a council function, and personal care charges are part of how it is paid for today, so the design matters to the council's finances.

source.name: Prime Minister's Office, Prime Minister Andy Burnham sets out plans for a new National Care Service, 29 September 2026

items.title: Transformed Labour Force Survey decision point
items.why: If ONS and users are ready, the process starts for a November 2027 switch of headline labour market data.

source.name: ONS, Labour market transformation: update on progress and plans, August 2026

items.title: First V Levels in Education, Finance and Digital
items.why: A new post-16 route alongside T Levels and A Levels.

source.name: DfE, New Vocational GCSEs unveiled, 23 September 2026

items.title: Planned switch of headline labour market data to the Transformed Labour Force Survey
items.why: Subject to readiness. Local and annual data follow from 2028.

source.name: ONS, Labour market transformation: update on progress and plans, August 2026

items.title: Every area to have, or be establishing, a strategic authority
items.why: The government's stated ambition, with strategic authorities in place everywhere by the end of 2028.

source.name: Cabinet Office, Rewiring the State: Cabinet Statement, 31 July 2026

items.title: Visitor levy revenue plans due from strategic authorities
items.why: The point by which NEMSA would set out how levy revenues are invested. We still need the borough's overnight-stay baseline.

source.name: Cabinet Office, Rewiring the State: Cabinet Statement, 31 July 2026

items.title: Mayors retain a share of local income tax
items.why: Replaces central grants. Receipts are retained locally from April 2028, with detail confirmed at the Spending Review.

source.name: Cabinet Office, Rewiring the State: Cabinet Statement, 31 July 2026

items.title: Local Innovation Partnerships Fund devolved to established mayors, NEMSA included
items.why: NEMSA decides how its share of local innovation funding is spent, the first dedicated research and development money held by mayors. It sits alongside the new Good Growth Funds, on which the Budget on 28 October is due to say more.
items.action: Ask NEMSA whether spending will be reported by local authority.

source.name: No.10, Prime Minister to hand regions innovation funding to build world-leading industries, 9 October 2026

items.title: New technical pathways from age 14 begin
items.why: Too late for today's 18 to 24 cohort, but it changes the route into work for the next one.

source.name: DfE, New Vocational GCSEs unveiled, 23 September 2026

pending_verification.claim: Pubs and hotels valuation review reports by the end of March 2027
pending_verification.note: Not found on the call-for-evidence page, which says only that findings will be published in a report. Find the source or drop. Re-checked 2 October 2026. MHCLG (10 September) says only that the review reports in time for decisions to be implemented at the next revaluation. Still no date.

pending_verification.claim: Jobs Guarantee national rollout starts in November 2026
pending_verification.note: The DWP page says later in 2026. Shown on the calendar as later in 2026 until a dated source appears. Re-checked 28 September 2026, the page still says later in 2026. Re-checked 2 October 2026, the page still says later in 2026.

pending_verification.claim: National Visitor Economy Strategy expected autumn 2026
pending_verification.note: No primary source for the timing found yet.

pending_verification.claim: Devolution white paper published with the Budget on 28 October
pending_verification.note: The Chancellor's 7 September speech confirms the fiscal devolution roadmap at the Budget, not a white paper. Find the source for the white paper or drop. Re-checked 2 October 2026. DfE (10 September) describes it only as forthcoming. Still no date. Re-checked 2 November 2026. None of the 64 Budget documents is a devolution white paper. The Red Book says the Rewiring the State Delivery Plan will be published before the end of the year (para 4.58), now on the calendar.

pending_verification.claim: Youth Matters Fund (£450m) opens for applications
pending_verification.note: DCMS says it will open soon. No date published as of 2 October 2026.

pending_verification.claim: NEMSA has opened a £6m events fund for the visitor economy
pending_verification.note: Not found on NEMSA's own site on 26 October 2026. Find NEMSA's announcement and closing date, or drop.

log.note: Seeded from every edition published since July 2026, each date checked at source, plus the ONS release calendar to March 2027 and the S&P Global calendar.

Full horizon scan run with the weekly edition. ONS calendar swept, no changes. S&P Global release dates re-checked. Every non-ONS item re-fetched at source and verified, none moved. Two pending claims promoted (14+ pathways from September 2028, May 2027 elections on existing boundaries) and two new pending added.

Full horizon scan run with the weekly edition, ahead of a twelve-day gap to the next edition on 14 October. ONS calendar swept, one release added (productivity flash, 16 February 2027). S&P Global release dates re-checked at source, all held dates unchanged. Every non-ONS item due within 60 days, and every provisional or expected item, re-fetched at source, and none moved. Innovation Fund dates re-confirmed in the bid pack after its 29 September update, which only corrected audio links. Eight items added from this week's sweep and one pending claim added.

Refresh from the Monthly Policy Update, October 2026. Eight items added from the edition, of which one (adult gaming centres needing planning permission from the start of 2027) promotes a pending claim now traced to the No.10 announcement of 11 August. Every consultation and funding deadline in the edition re-read at source on 2 October, none moved. Two pending notes updated, the pubs and hotels report date and the devolution white paper, both still undated.

Refresh from the 14 October catch-up What's New. ONS sweep added 2 releases, confirmed 4 (the Blue Book 2026, travel trends and two inflation releases) and retired 3 to the archive. The Council Tax Base return moved from 9 to 16 October. The 16 December BRES entry reworded, because the calendar does not say how it relates to the 18 November release. Every non-ONS deadline within 60 days re-read at source, none moved. Nine items added from the edition. Pending list unchanged, all seven still without a primary dated source.

Refresh from the 19 October What's New. ONS sweep added 6 releases and retired 7 to the archive, none moved. Every non-ONS deadline within 60 days re-read at source and the S&P Global calendar re-checked, none moved. Eleven items added from the edition, including five S&P Global November releases (one was already held), the employment status consultation (promoted from the pending list), the school exclusion call for evidence, the supported housing licensing consultation and the carbon border tax start. Four items marked published and the British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme entry retitled to applications close.

Refresh from the 26 October What's New. ONS sweep added 1 release, moved 2 (subregional productivity 2024 from 5 to 24 November, regional international trade 2024 from 10 November to 15 December, both postponed by ONS) and retired 8 to the archive. Every gov.uk-sourced item within 60 days re-checked, with the Employment Rights Act timeline re-read because the page changed, none moved. Nine items added from the edition, including the Green Book reforms at the Budget, four consultations and calls for evidence, two release announcements and the extended legacy local plan deadline and the Innovation Fund second round. Jobs Guarantee and Innovation Fund entries updated. Items from the window marked published. NEMSA events fund lead added to the pending list.

Standalone horizon scan after the Budget. ONS sweep confirmed the provisional mid-2026 population estimate for 26 November at 09:30 and retired 7 items to the archive. 26 items added: 12 dated commitments from the Budget documents (including the Household Energy Payment, Your First Home, the Rewiring the State Delivery Plan, the National Procurement Policy Statement, the International Investment Summit and the Derelict Buildings Fund guidance, with Gateshead's £1.91m allocation), 11 consultations and calls for evidence from the gov.uk sweep, two S&P Global releases and the April 2027 MPC decision. Hope on the High Street and the PPN 026 guidance marked published on 28 October. Business rates retention and BICS entries re-sourced to the Red Book. Disabled people employment statistics confirmed for 4 November. Every gov.uk item within 60 days and every provisional or expected gov.uk item re-read at source, none moved. Bank of England and S&P Global calendars re-checked, none moved. Complete regional GVA 2024 still not released. Items from the last 14 days were already marked published by the sweep. Derelict Buildings Fund lead promoted from the pending list.
